title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A retired Georgia couple was defrauded of nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency investment scam that exploited trust built through incremental withdrawals and false returns. The scammers used a real trading app but presented the victims with a fake AI-generated website that displayed fabricated account balances and transaction history. The deception persisted until the couple attempted a larger withdrawal and found their funds inaccessible.

This is a case of impersonation and screen manipulation rather than a failure of the AI system itself. The criminals generated a convincing fake interface to show victims what they wanted to see, not what the actual trading app contained. No human verification occurred before the couple transferred their money, and no safeguard caught the discrepancy between what they viewed and what actually existed in their accounts.

It is not established whether the trading app had security features that would have alerted users to the mismatch, or what opportunities existed to verify account details through channels outside the compromised display.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a mobile trading app, gradually building trust by allowing small withdrawals and modest returns. Over time, Jerry increased his investments, believing he was making legitimate profits. The scam unraveled when he attempted a larger withdrawal and discovered he could not access his money.

The scammers had created a fake artificial intelligence-generated website that displayed false account information to the couple. Gwinnett County police confirmed the trading app itself was real, but criminals manipulated what the victims saw on their screens. Jerry and Mindy Dunaway are now warning others about the sophistication of such schemes. Police indicate victims rarely recover their funds in these cases, though the couple is working with investigators. Their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help them cover daily expenses.
